Hotel performance in the Miami Beach submarket
achieved modest gains. Through October 2025, the
submarket recorded 12-month RevPAR growth of 1.6%,
driven by a -0.9% occupancy change and a 0.3% ADR
gain. Although transient demand has retreated recently,
incremental group volume, resulting from a series of
events, contributed to the RevPAR performance.
The positive momentum is anticipated to continue in the
next several months, albeit to a lesser degree. The 12-
month RevPAR is projected to change by 0.0% by year-
end, driven by minor rate growth offsetting occupancy
declines. Supply additions are estimated to outpace
demand growth, resulting in reduced occupied rooms.
For comparison, the Miami market RevPAR calls for
1.1% growth by year-end.
Although the nation is anticipated to suffer from tough
hurricane and wildfire comps, reduced demand levels,
and stagnant rate growth, the 2026 outlook for Miami
Beach remains favorable due to the submarket's rate
strength, as affluent consumers continue to spend on
lodging during times of uncertainty.
However, several factors could adversely affect the
submarket forecast. Negative impacts from tariffs,
ranging from lower consumer sentiment influencing
leisure travel decisions to reduced business activities
affecting group bookings, could dampen the submarket's
outlook. Additionally, reduced international inbound travel
could hinder demand projections for Miami Beach.
Historically, February is one of the busiest months during
South Florida's peak tourist season. For Miami Beach,
events such as the Miami International Boat Show and
South Beach Wine and Food Festival attract tens of
thousands of visitors annually. In addition, the Miami
International Auto Show in September and Art Basel
Miami Beach in December bring significant attendees to
the Miami Beach Convention Center.
Furthermore, Miami is expected to host seven games
during the FIFA World Cup 2026, including four group-
stage games, a round of 32, a round of 16, and a third-
place playoff. The series of events will contribute to the
demand for area hotels.
The Miami International Airport (MIA) also helps drive
hotel demand in the submarket. Year-to-date through
August 2025, the airport served nearly 37.9 million
travelers, representing a -1.4% decrease year-over-
year. International passenger traffic typically accounts for
almost half of total passenger volume. The airport is
ranked the second busiest in Florida, just behind Orlando
International Airport.
Approximately 1,300 rooms across 4 hotels are under
construction in Miami Beach, representing 5.7% of the
existing inventory. Roughly 220 rooms are anticipated to
open by year-end, including the 147-room Miami Beach
Hotel, formerly known as Thompson Miami Beach.
Nearly 1,300 rooms are in final planning across seven
projects.
Year-to-date through October 2025, eight hotels were
sold for a combined sales volume of $239 million. One
significant transaction, the sale of the stalled Rosewood
The Raleigh Miami Beach project, accounted for over
85% of the deal volume.
